turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on in, sit yourself down. You look a bit washed out, so what's brought you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm just wrecked. That's why I'm here. I can't even do the stairs at home without stopping halfway.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Wrecked as in tired, or is the breathing the bit that's worrying you?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): The tiredness, mostly. I'm snapping at my flatmate over nothing. And yeah the stairs, one flight and I'm gasping.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long have you been this tired?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): I keep eating ice. Like proper cubes out of the freezer, all evening. It's ridiculous, I know.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, the ice, we'll come back to that. The tiredness, how long is it actually going on?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, I haven't a notion of the exact day. A couple of months, anyway. It just crept up.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the gasping on the stairs, did that come on around the same time?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Flat ground I'm grand. On the stairs I have to stop and hold the rail, and it eases if I stand still a minute.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any cough with it?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No cough.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you had a fever?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I am freezing all the time though, even with the heating on I'm in a jumper.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Has your weight dropped at all?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Well, actually, I think it has a bit. My belt's on a tighter hole. I couldn't tell you how much, uh, I don't own a scales.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Grand, we won't hang anything on a number we haven't got. Your periods, are they heavy or all over the place?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): They're normal. Why, did someone say they weren't? Every twenty eight days, five days, not heavy, same as always.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Nobody said a word. I'm only asking because heavy periods can leave you drained. The ice, then, how long have you been at that?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): A few weeks. Err, maybe three. I go through a whole tray a night. My flatmate thinks I've lost the plot.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you eat meat or fish at all?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I'm vegetarian, strict, six years now, no meat and no fish. Pasta, cheese, beans sometimes, and a fierce lot of tea.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any tablets or vitamins on the go at the minute?

[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): I got ferrous sulphait tablets from the chemist, uh, maybe 200 milligrams, once a day. I only lasted three days, my stomach was in bits, so I stopped. That was last month.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stopped completely? Nothing else, no iron water, no multivitamin?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing else. And I'm not starting them again, they were brutal.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): I wouldn't push a tablet that turned your stomach, not before we know what we're at. Did the stomach settle once you stopped?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, grand after a day or two. Can we hurry this on, I'm on an early shift tomorrow and I'm wrecked sitting here.

[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll keep it moving. I'm just thinking out loud, err, tiredness, the ice craving, breathless on the stairs, strict vegetarian, it lines up with low iron. That's a working impression, not a fact yet.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): So I'm anaemic. Brilliant.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Maybe. I can't call it anaemia until the bloods are back. Low B12 can look similar enough if you don't eat meat, so I wouldn't rule that out either.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): I eat cheese. Does that not cover it?

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cheese has a little B12, not always enough, and it does nothing for the iron. Tea with your meals actually blocks the iron you do get from food. That's the bit I'd like you to change.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Change how. I'm not going back to meat, if that's where this is heading.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): You don't have to. Lentils, beans, the greens, have them with orange juice or a bit of fruit, and leave the tea for an hour either side of the meal.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. Whatever.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me have a quick look at you before you head off. Sleeve up there, please.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure is 112 over 70. Pulse is 98, a touch fast for sitting still. Oxygen is 99 percent.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Is 98 bad?
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not dangerous, just quicker than I'd like in a young one at rest. The inner eyelids are pale. Chest is clear, no wheeze. Heart sounds are normal, I don't hear a murmur.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Pale. So it's the iron thing again.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): It fits, it doesn't prove it. I'll send bloods today, a full blood count, a ferritin, and B12 and folate as well.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Today? I have a bus to get.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Phlebotomy is just down the corridor, a few minutes and you're away. The results should be back for a visit in a fortnight.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): A fortnight. Can you not just ring me?

[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'd rather see you. Two weeks, here, and we'll go through the numbers properly. If you feel faint, or the breathing gets markedly worse before that, don't sit on it, come back or go to the emergency department.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. Two weeks. And the tea thing.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes. Food first, and no new tablet from me today. If the ferritin is low we can talk about a gentler iron then, but I'm not starting one now.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand. I'm going before I fall asleep on this chair.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Get the bloods done on your way out, and mind yourself on those stairs.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, yeah. I heard you the first time.

spec.situation: Tired young woman, strict vegetarian, breathless on stairs, craving ice; periods normal by her account; blood tests planned; diet advice.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).
